name: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace
insider_take: This isn't just a hotel—it's a reborn Art Nouveau masterpiece that once hosted European royalty and now stands as Budapest's most prestigious address.
whats_special: Built in 1906 as the original Gresham Palace, this Four Seasons occupies one of Europe's finest examples of Art Nouveau architecture. The building's stunning Zsolnay ceramic tiles, original mosaics, and wrought-iron Peacock Gates have been meticulously restored to their former glory. Located directly on the Danube riverfront, it offers unparalleled views of the Chain Bridge and Buda Castle.
pro_tip: Request a room on the Danube side for postcard-perfect views of the illuminated Chain Bridge and Buda Castle at night—the sight is absolutely magical and worth the upgrade.
dont_miss: The hotel's magnificent lobby with its original stained-glass dome and the peaceful inner courtyard. Step outside to explore the nearby Chain Bridge (just steps away) and take the funicular up to Buda Castle. The famous Széchenyi Thermal Baths are a 15-minute drive for an authentic Budapest spa experience.
pros: Historic Art Nouveau palace building with stunning architectural details
Prime location on the Danube River with panoramic views of Buda Castle
Exceptional Four Seasons service standards and amenities
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflecting exclusive location and brand
Historic building constraints may limit some modern amenities
